title: Relative Hom evaluation and its transport map for a family of functors
statement:
Use quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets, coherent transformations and right-pinched mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the arrow mapping complexes $U_C(a,c)$ and right-pinch maps $j_{C,a,c}$ of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], and the coherent Hom bifunctors and specified arrow-fibration transport of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. Work in a fixed universe $\mathcal W$ and a containing universe for categories of $\mathcal W$-small objects. Let $B,C,E$ be $\mathcal W$-small quasicategories, $K$ a $\mathcal W$-small simplicial set, and let
$$i:B\to C,\qquad t:B\to E,\qquad T:K\times C\to E$$
be simplicial maps satisfying the equality $T\circ(\mathrm{id}_K\times i)=t\circ\operatorname{pr}_B$ on $K\times B$. Thus the entire restriction to $K\times B$, including its higher simplices, is independent of $K$. For $b\in B$, $c\in C$, put $M_{b,c}=\operatorname{Map}_C(i(b),c)$ and let $q^T_{b,c}:A^T_{b,c}\to K$ be the pullback along $T(-,c)$ of the source-fixed arrow left fibration of $E$ with source $t(b)$. Define a map over $K$
$$\Phi_{b,c}:K\times U_C(i(b),c)\longrightarrow A^T_{b,c}$$
by the following simplex formula: if $h:\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to C$ has constant endpoints $i(b),c$ and $k:\Delta^n\to K$, its arrow coordinate is $(z,s)\mapsto T(k(z),h(z,s))$. The base coordinate is $k$.

There is a coherent natural transformation, in the infinity category of functors from $B^{\mathrm{op}}\times C$ to $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S_{\mathcal W})$,
$$\varepsilon_{b,c}:\Delta_K H_C(i(b),c)\longrightarrow H_E(t(b),T(-,c)).$$
The Hom/arrow transport comparisons can be chosen coherently in $b,c$ so that the image of $\varepsilon_{b,c}$ under the mapping-space comparison of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] is the map $\Phi_{b,c}\circ(\mathrm{id}_K\times j_{C,i(b),c})$, after identifying $H_C(i(b),c)$ with $M_{b,c}$. This is an identification in the full space of maps over $K$, with its higher homotopies, and is compatible with arbitrary simplicial parameters and pullback along maps $K'\to K$. These comparisons are compatible with enlargement of the containing universe.

In particular, for an edge $u:c\to c'$ of $C$, the naturality square has upper map $\Delta_K(u\circ-)$, lower map the coherent postcomposition transformation $H_E(t(b),T(-,u))$, and vertical maps $\varepsilon_{b,c},\varepsilon_{b,c'}$. It commutes with its coherent homotopy in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S_{\mathcal W})$. The analogous square for precomposition along an edge of $B$ holds as well. The postcomposition square, including its transport identification, is valid for parameterized families of composable arrows and retains the data on $K\times\Delta^1$ and all higher simplices. No equivalence assertion about $\varepsilon$ or about spaces of sections is made. Empty $K$ and empty mapping spaces are allowed.

Corollary 8.3.5.8 (046J) and Remark 8.3.5.9 (03PD) give single-functor Hom compatibility; the relative assertion above is an additional lemma, not a verbatim consequence stated there.
